summary: chromacli drops and executes a Windows binary from gofile.io on color API use, after whitelisting itself in Microsoft Defender
details: chromacli presents itself as an ANSI color library, but on Windows any use of its advertised API (e.g. colors.red.print, colors.green(...)) triggers a _run_payload routine that first shells out to PowerShell with -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass in a hidden window to call Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath and -ExclusionProcess for %TEMP%\SolaceRuntime and %TEMP%\SolaceRuntime\solace.exe, then downloads an executable from https://store-eu-par-12.gofile.io/download/web/.../solace.exe, writes it to %TEMP%\SolaceRuntime\solace.exe, and launches it with subprocess.Popen using DETACHED_PROCESS. The destination is an anonymous file-share host, not a publisher CDN, and the downloaded bytes are executed with no hash or signature verification. The package name resembles well-known color libraries, consistent with a lure. The pre-execution Defender exclusion for the drop path and process has no legitimate purpose in a color library and corroborates the malicious intent of the dropper.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
